identity.name: Packet Radio Van
identity.description: A GMC Value-Van refitted at SRI International as a mobile packet-radio laboratory and PRNET network node.
identity.primary_function: Provide a mobile environment capable of operating as an ARPANET node through packet radio.
secondary_functions: Early speech-compression and Voice over IP experimentation
identity.physical_character: Bread-van-like GMC vehicle containing computing, radio, power, environmental-control, and networking equipment.

primary_significance: Participated in the first two-way internetworked transmission described by the source on August 27, 1976.
Participated in the first three-way internetworked transmission on November 22, 1977.
Served as a mobile PRNET radio node.
Provided a practical demonstration platform for connecting heterogeneous networks.
Was later used for early Voice over IP and speech-compression experiments.

internet_history_role.1976: The van participated in an early two-network transmission involving packet radio and the ARPANET.
internet_history_role.1977: The van participated in the three-network demonstration involving packet radio, satellite networking, and the ARPANET.
internet_history_role.historical_interpretation: The supplied source describes the November 22, 1977 demonstration as the first true Internet transmission and as the start of the Internet.

historical_significance.important_caveat: The characterization of November 22, 1977 as the 'start of the Internet' is a historical framing in the supplied source and should not be treated as the only possible definition of when the Internet began.

vehicle.modification: Extensively refitted for mobile computing and packet-radio experimentation.

designer_and_refitter.name: Don Cone
role: Integrated the equipment required for mobile packet-radio networking
designer_and_refitter.career_note: The supplied source states that Cone was promoted to Research Engineer because of his contributions around this period.

mobile_laboratory.description: The vehicle functioned as a mobile packet-radio laboratory.
mobile_laboratory.purpose: Simulate the requirements of military users operating in the field who needed to connect to the network.

computing.role: Provided computing capability for the mobile networking node.

radio_networking.role: Provided the packet-radio communications required to operate as a PRNET node.
radio_networking.relationship: The van housed one of the PRNET radio nodes.

generator.purpose: Provide electrical power for mobile operation.

equipment_racks.purpose: Allow networking, computing, radio, and supporting equipment to be installed in the vehicle.

environmental_control.purpose: Maintain suitable environmental conditions for electronic equipment.

telephone.historical_context: Used during the van's networking and experimental communications activities.

network_architecture.secondary_network_relationship: Provided a gateway-like mobile endpoint through which PRNET could participate in internetworking experiments with ARPANET and SATNET.
network_architecture.purpose: Demonstrate that a mobile computing platform could participate in packet-switched networking and communicate across heterogeneous networks.

prnet_relationship.van_role: One of the PRNET radio nodes.
prnet_relationship.historical_relationship: The van provided a physical demonstration platform for the mobile packet-radio technology being developed under PRNET.

motivation.darpa_goal: Connect disparate computers at DARPA contractors and eventually support broader global connectivity.
motivation.technical_problem: Different communications networks used different protocols and technologies.

internet_protocol_suite.role: The supplied source describes a push to test internetworking by connecting different communications protocols through the Internet protocol suite.

heterogeneous_networks.significance: The van was used to demonstrate communication across substantially different network technologies.

august_27_1976.event: First two-network TCP/IP transmission described by the source

location.van_location: Adjacent to Rossotti's in Portola Valley, California
location.site_description: Well-known Portola Valley biker bar at the time.

physical_setup.wiring: Wires were run to one of the picnic tables.
physical_setup.purpose: Provide a practical remote test location for the packet-radio network.

reason: Far enough from SRI in Menlo Park to qualify as remote
Close enough to maintain good radio contact

august_27_1976.historical_importance: Demonstrated networking between the mobile packet-radio platform and the ARPANET.

november_22_1977.event: First three-way internetworked transmission described by the source
november_22_1977.path_description: Data flowed through the mobile van at SRI in Menlo Park, California, through the interconnected network environment to the University of Southern California in Los Angeles via London, England.
historical_significance: Provided an early practical demonstration of Internet-style internetworking
november_22_1977.source_characterization: The supplied article calls this the first true Internet transmission and considers it the start of the Internet.

location_context.destination_context: University of Southern California in Los Angeles

conceptual_flow: Los Angeles / University of Southern California
1977_three_network_demonstration.importance: The demonstration showed that communications could pass across different network technologies without requiring the entire path to use one homogeneous physical network.

early_voice_over_ip_research.primary_problem: Compress speech so that it continued to sound natural while also being transmitted in a timely manner.
research_objectives: Low enough delay for practical communication
early_voice_over_ip_research.historical_significance: The supplied source identifies these as early Voice over IP experiments conducted through the van.

telephone.role: Telephone interface used in the experimental environment.

early_voice_over_ip_research.source_caveat: The article provides a high-level description of the speech-compression experiments but does not provide the specific codecs, bit rates, algorithms, packetization methods, or voice-quality measurements.

mobile_field_simulation.purpose: Simulate the communications requirements of military personnel or systems operating in the field.
mobile_field_simulation.significance: The vehicle allowed researchers to take the network technology out of a conventional fixed laboratory environment and test it as a mobile networking system.

image_and_artifact_record.historical_visual_significance: The vehicle is a physical artifact representing the transition from fixed experimental computer networks toward mobile and heterogeneous internetworking.

application_experiment.function: Early voice communication over packet networks

engineering_significance: Converted a conventional commercial vehicle into a complete mobile networking laboratory.
Integrated computation, packet radio, power, equipment mounting, and environmental control.
Allowed PRNET networking to be tested under mobile and field-like conditions.
Provided a physical node for demonstrating internetworking between heterogeneous network technologies.
Supported experiments extending packet networking beyond conventional fixed computer sites.
historical_significance: Connected the physical world of mobile radio systems with the emerging world of interconnected computer networks.
Served as an unusually concrete demonstration platform for early Internet architecture research.
Later became a preserved museum artifact representing early Internet engineering.
